problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. The available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 5 cubic meters, revenue $182
* Container 2: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $77
* Container 3: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $68
* Container 4: volume 8 cubic meters, revenue $118
* Container 5: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $99

* Container 12: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue $50
* Container 13: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $255
* Container 14: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue $46
* Container 15: volume 38 cubic meters, revenue $187
* Container 16: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue $10
* Container 17: volume 38 cubic meters, revenue $166
* Container 18: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $98
* Container 19: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $19
* Container 20: volume 35 cubic meters, revenue $249
* Container 21: volume 50 cubic meters, revenue $279
* Container 22: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue $125
* Container 23: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $81
* Container 24: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue $197
* Container 25: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue $270
* Container 26: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue $92
* Container 27: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $48
* Container 28: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $265
* Container 29: volume 24 cubic meters, revenue $251
* Container 30: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue $223

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 595 cubic meters. Determine which containers to load to maximize total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
